_doc: The custom family: any section given as a closed outline, with its area, second moments, torsion constant and mass worked out from that outline. A custom profile is its outline: a set of your own with family custom, and its outline beside it as rules/outlines/<the set's name>.json (source, licence, and loops of [x, y] points in mm about the middle of the section's envelope: the outside of the metal, then each hole). cad measure <model> --profile <name> writes both from a model or a DXF. This set is the kit's own example, a 30 x 30 x 3 mm T section drawn for the kit, so the family can be tried: profileModel('custom', { width, height, material }, { outline }) takes any other. The drawn outline leaves out nothing: it is the outline.
name: profile-custom

family.rule: A section given by its outline
family.source: a starting value of the kit's: give your own with profileModel(family, { width, height, wall, material }) or in a set of your own

width.rule: Across the example's envelope: its outline is 30 wide. A custom profile's width and height are its outline's, and the check says so where they differ
width.source: a starting value of the kit's: give your own with profileModel(family, { width, height, wall, material }) or in a set of your own

height.source: a starting value of the kit's: give your own with profileModel(family, { width, height, wall, material }) or in a set of your own

material.rule: Extruded aluminium, EN AW-6063 T5: one of the alloys such sections are extruded in (6060 and 6063 in Europe, 6061 and 6063 in America). Name the alloy on your supplier's sheet where it matters
material.source: a starting value of the kit's: give your own with profileModel(family, { width, height, wall, material }) or in a set of your own
